title: Voicemail, Email, Portal, and Secure Communication

sections.learningObjectives:
- Use voicemail, email, and patient portals professionally and in accordance with office policy.
- Protect protected health information (PHI) in electronic communication by applying the minimum necessary standard and appropriate safeguards.
- Choose secure communication channels, including encryption and patient portals, and avoid insecure channels such as standard SMS.
- Recognize and escalate urgent or clinical messages, security incidents, and potential breaches to the appropriate staff.
- Document electronic and telephone communications accurately and completely as part of the patient record.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

The greeting is like a sign on a store door that says the name of the store, when it is open, and asks visitors to leave a note with their name and phone number.

### Question 2

It is like writing a phone number on a sticky note in big, neat handwriting and reading it back so your friend can copy it without mistakes.

### Question 3

When you leave a note for a friend, you only write what they need to know, like call me back, and not their private secrets where anyone could read them.

### Question 4

It is like telling a friend the time and place of a party and how to text you back, without reading them a long list of private details.

### Question 5

It is like checking the mailbox every day instead of once a month, so important letters are not left sitting and forgotten.

### Question 6

If a friend asks a question only a doctor can answer, you do not guess; you write down the question and pass it to the doctor.

### Question 7

It is like putting a note on the door that says closed today and tells visitors who to call in an emergency.

### Question 8

It is like writing a homework note with the person's name, the date, and what they need, so the teacher can help them correctly.

### Question 9

You would not announce a friend's secret where anyone could hear it; you would just ask them to call you back.

### Question 10

It is like speaking to a guest kindly and clearly so they feel welcome and know exactly what to do next.

### Question 11

If a friend asks to borrow something that only a parent can approve, you pass the request to the parent instead of saying yes yourself.

### Question 12

It is like a clear sign that says the store name, its open hours, and asks you to leave a note with your name and number.

### Question 13

It is like reading a phone number out loud twice so your friend can check the digits before hanging up.

### Question 14

A safe note says only please call me back, like leaving a friend a message that says call me without telling their secrets.

### Question 15

Before mailing a secret note, you double-check the address and make sure the person said it was okay to send it.

### Question 16

A subject line is like writing the title of a book on the cover so people know what is inside without opening it.

### Question 17

Before mailing a letter, you check the envelope to make sure the name and address are right.

### Question 18

When helping with one part of a project, you only share the pages you need, not the whole stack of papers.

### Question 19

If a stranger hands you a mystery drink and says drink this, you do not taste it; you tell a trusted adult instead.

### Question 20

Signing an email is like signing your name at the end of a letter so the person knows who wrote it.

### Question 21

Sending unencrypted email is like mailing a postcard where anyone who handles it can read what is written.

### Question 22

The portal is like a locked mailbox that only the patient can open with their own key, instead of leaving the letter where anyone can grab it.

### Question 23

Important notes from a patient are like pages in a file that should be kept safely, not thrown away.

### Question 24

If you accidentally mail a private letter to the wrong house, you tell a trusted adult right away instead of pretending it did not happen.

### Question 25

When you have a note for one friend, you hand it only to that friend instead of reading it aloud to the whole room.

### Question 26

A patient portal is like a private website with a special login where patients can read their own health notes and send secure messages.

### Question 27

Before handing someone a key to a private locker, you make sure they are really the owner of that locker.

### Question 28

The portal is like leaving a note for the teacher; if there is a fire, you do not leave a note, you call for help right away.

### Question 29

If a friend says their chest hurts and they cannot breathe, you call 911 right away instead of waiting.

### Question 30

Questions about test results are like math problems only the teacher can check, so you hand them to the teacher, not guess.

### Question 31

A password is like the secret code to your diary; you do not say it out loud where others can hear.

### Question 32

The portal is like a locked drop box at a bank, safe for important papers, instead of leaving them on a public bench.

### Question 33

The portal is like a locked room that only people with the right key card can enter.

### Question 34

If you forget the code to your bike lock, you use the official way to get a new code, not borrow someone else's.

### Question 35

A standard text is like writing on a whiteboard in a shared room; other people might see it.

### Question 36

Results go in the patient's locked mailbox, not written on a postcard for anyone to read.

### Question 37

Encryption is like writing a secret in a code that only you and your friend know how to unscramble.

### Question 38

At rest is like locking papers in a safe; in transit is like putting them in a locked box while the mail truck carries them.

### Question 39

You give a helper only the one page they need for their job, not your whole notebook.

### Question 40

PHI is like a person's name written next to their private health story; together they become protected.

### Question 41

The Security Rule is like a list of rules for locking up electronic health information so only the right people can see it.

### Question 42

A password is like a toothbrush; you do not share it and you keep it to yourself.

### Question 43

Locking your screen is like closing and locking your diary when you leave the room.

### Question 44

If you see a pipe leaking, you tell the building manager right away instead of waiting for the floor to flood.

### Question 45

Before mailing a letter, you check the address so it goes to the right mailbox.

### Question 46

A BAA is like making a repair person sign a promise to keep your house safe while they work inside it.

### Question 47

Doctors caring for the same patient can share what they need to do their jobs, like teammates passing the ball during a game.

### Question 48

Writing please keep out on a paper bag does not lock it; anyone can still reach inside.

### Question 49

The subject line is like the outside of an envelope; you write just enough to identify it, not the secret inside.

### Question 50

An auto-reply is like a note on your locker that anyone can read, so you only write safe, general information.

### Question 51

Use the special walkie-talkie the office gives you, not a toy one from home, when talking about private patient things.

### Question 52

MFA is like needing both a key and a secret knock to open the clubhouse door.

### Question 53

You would not shout a friend's secret in the hallway where everyone can hear it.

### Question 54

You lock the box and check the address before mailing important papers.

### Question 55

You read the note the friend sent, answer kindly, and remind them to use the locked mailbox next time.

### Question 56

The portal is like a private chat room that needs a special key to enter, not a big public square.

### Question 57

Important papers are delivered in a locked way and only after checking the person is really who they say they are.

### Question 58

You close and lock your diary whenever you leave the table so no one else can read it.

### Question 59

If a stranger sends you a link and says click here, you check with a trusted adult first instead of clicking.

### Question 60

If a friend sends you a question, you answer soon instead of leaving them waiting for days.

### Question 61

You follow the rulebook and ask the coach when you are not sure which play to run.

### Question 62

If you leave a note that says call me back but forget who it is for, the person may not know it is meant for them.

### Question 63

The name plus the illness together is like writing a person's secret on the outside of the envelope.

### Question 64

You use the special office binder for important papers instead of your personal notebook that anyone might find.

### Question 65

You tilt your notebook so the person next to you cannot read what you are writing.

### Question 66

You use the office's official announcement system instead of shouting everyone's private schedule in the hallway.

### Question 67

It is like a friend saying it is okay to tell their mom the full message because they trust her.

### Question 68

Writing professionally is like speaking kindly and clearly so the reader understands and feels respected.

### Question 69

If you get a mystery package, you do not open it; you tell a trusted adult so they can check it safely.

### Question 70

When the locked mailbox is not an option, you use another approved locked method, never a box with no lock.

### Question 71

You use the office's special secure phone line for private messages, not your own phone.

### Question 72

Before sharing a secret, you make sure you are really talking to the right person and not a stranger pretending to be them.

### Question 73

You write down what you sent, to whom, and when, like keeping a careful log of important letters.

### Question 74

You check the address on the package and call to make sure it arrived at the right house.

### Question 75

Access controls are like giving each person a key that only opens the doors they need to enter.

### Question 76

If you drop your friend's private papers in the hallway, you pick them up and tell a grown-up right away.

### Question 77

The portal is for checking your own homework and asking the teacher a question, not for emergencies.

### Question 78

To set up a playdate, you share the time and place, not your friend's entire diary.

### Question 79

You use a screen cover and keep your notebook with you so no one can peek at your private writing.

### Question 80

You only deliver private papers the official, locked way, even if the person asks for a quicker shortcut.

### Question 81

Secure messaging is like passing notes in a locked box with a secret code, not in the open.

### Question 82

You only share a friend's secret with someone if your friend said that person is allowed to know.

### Question 83

Using BCC is like sending a group note without showing everyone's home address to the whole group.

### Question 84

If a teammate is doing something unsafe, you kindly remind them of the safe way and tell the coach if they keep doing it.

### Question 85

We lock up private things because they are private, and because the rules say we must keep them safe.
